verses.text: While Jeremiah was still locked up in the courtyard of the guard, the LORD's message came to him a second time:
"This is what the LORD says, the LORD who made the earth, who formed it and set it in place. The LORD is his name:
'Call to me, and I will answer you. I will tell you great and hidden things that you do not know.'
For this is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says about the houses of this city and the palaces of the kings of Judah, which have been torn down to defend against the siege ramps and the sword:

'People are coming to fight the Babylonians, but the houses will be filled with the dead bodies of those I will kill in my anger and fury. I have turned my face away from this city because of all its wickedness.
But look, I will bring health and healing to it. I will heal my people and let them enjoy great peace and security.
I will bring Judah and Israel back from captivity and rebuild them as they were before.
I will make them clean from all the sin they have committed against me. I will forgive all their sins and their rebellion against me.

Then this city will bring me joy, praise, and honor before all the nations of the earth. They will hear about all the good things I do for it, and they will tremble in awe at all the good and the peace I give it.'"

This is what the LORD says: "You say about this place, 'It is a ruin, with no people or animals.' The towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem are empty, with no people or animals living there. But in this place you will hear once again

the sounds of joy and gladness, the voices of bride and groom, and the voices of people bringing thank offerings to the LORD's temple, saying, 'Give thanks to the LORD of Armies, for the LORD is good. His faithful love lasts forever.' For I will bring the land back from captivity as it was before," says the LORD.
This is what the LORD of Armies says: "In this place, now a ruin with no people or animals, and in all its towns, there will again be pastures where shepherds rest their flocks.

In the towns of the hill country, the western foothills, and the Negev, in the land of Benjamin, in the villages around Jerusalem, and in the towns of Judah, flocks will again pass under the hand of the one who counts them," says the LORD.
"Look, the days are coming," says the LORD, "when I will keep the good promise I made to the people of Israel and the people of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will make a righteous Branch grow from David's family. He will do what is fair and right in the land.
In those days Judah will be saved, and Jerusalem will live in safety. This is the name it will be called: The LORD Our Righteousness."
For this is what the LORD says: "David will never fail to have a descendant sitting on the throne of Israel.
And the Levitical priests will never fail to have someone standing before me to offer burnt offerings, burn grain offerings, and make sacrifices every day."
The LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"This is what the LORD says: 'If you could break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night, so that day and night no longer came at their set times,
then my covenant with my servant David could be broken, and he would have no descendant to rule on his throne. So could my covenant with the Levitical priests who serve me.
Just as the stars in the sky cannot be counted and the sand on the seashore cannot be measured, so I will make the descendants of my servant David and the Levites who serve me too many to count.'"
The LORD's message came to Jeremiah:
"Have you noticed what these people are saying? 'The LORD has rejected the two families he chose.' So they look down on my people and no longer think of them as a nation."
This is what the LORD says: "If I had not made my covenant with day and night, and set the laws of heaven and earth,

then I would reject the descendants of Jacob and of my servant David, and not choose any of David's descendants to rule over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. But I will bring them back from captivity and have mercy on them."
